intro: Handwriting to text turns handwriting into text: lecture notes, old letters, family recipes, meeting notes, diaries or forms filled in with a pen. Upload a photo or a scanned PDF and download the transcription as Word, text or Markdown to edit it, search it or copy it.

The transcription is done by a free AI model that understands images, through OpenRouter. It copies the text word for word, without correcting spelling or summarising, and marks what cannot be read as [illegible]. You can set the language of the text to help the model and choose whether the original line breaks are kept or paragraphs are joined.

Each page is one AI request and a task accepts up to 10 pages. It works best with sharp, well-lit photos taken straight on; if the handwriting is very hard or the paper very worn, the transcription may contain errors, so check it against the original.

If at some point there is no free model that accepts images, the tool switches itself off and tells you on this page; it becomes available again as soon as there is one. Images are sent to the model only to transcribe them, with your consent, and are deleted when they expire.
steps: Upload a photo or a scanned PDF (up to 10 pages).

faq.q: Does it work for printed text?
faq.a: Yes, but for printed text Image to text or OCR PDF are better, and they do not use AI requests.
Because the model could not read that part reliably. A sharper or closer photo usually helps.
Because right now there is no free model that accepts images. It switches back on when there is one.
